gap: No result ChatGPT got says what it costs to reach the 8–16 GB of RAM it recommends. TerraMaster's own 16 GB DDR5 module sells for $469.99 at the maker's store (read 2026-11-13). That is more than a whole UGREEN DXP2800 ($389.99) and the same as a TerraMaster F2-425 Plus with 8 GB already fitted ($469.99). Synology's DS725+ and DS925+ ship with only 4 GB, so 'buy it and add RAM later' is the expensive route; the cheaper route is a box that ships with the RAM.
standout_why: I compared against rackdiff.com (Paperless NAS vs VPS), peira.dev (Paperless NAS playbook) and racksandwatts.com (homelab NAS picks, checked 2026-10-25). ChatGPT also cited the Paperless-ngx setup, configuration and FAQ docs and showed answer cards. rackdiff gives RAM tiers but no NAS prices. peira names no hardware. racksandwatts lists RAM ceilings (DS225+ at 2 GB starting / 6 GB max) but only says 'Check price on Amazon'. ChatGPT's own answers say '16 GB preferred' and 'I'd upgrade the RAM to at least 8 GB' (on the DS925+) without pricing the upgrade. None of these pages prices a RAM module or compares how much RAM each box ships with against its price.
decides: It supports the low-cost picks that ship with enough RAM (UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99; TerraMaster F2-425 Plus at $469.99 with 8 GB) over 'buy a 4 GB Synology and upgrade'. It also puts the TerraMaster F4-424 Pro in a new light: at $759.99 it ships with 32 GB DDR5, so for a heavy OCR backlog it is the only box here priced with its RAM already in it. ChatGPT showed it at $773.99. For the Synology picks, Synology's own spec pages say NVMe storage pools need Synology-verified SSDs. That matters because every ChatGPT answer recommends PostgreSQL on an SSD volume.
